newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 4.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 4.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Germany's central advertising association (ZAW)defends advertising for alcoholic products. It rejects the argument that ads lead to more drinking among young people, citing a study by the Infratest institute showing the percentage of 15 to 17 year olds who regularly drink alcohol has dropped to 20 percent from 60 percent in recent years. (Horizont)
STUTTGART - Deutsche Bahn AG, the German railways company, is considering introducing stereos, televisions and telephones on domestic trains to make them more attractive for passengers.
(Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Deutsche Telekom AG, responding to news its cable television operations were being investigated by German cartel authorities, denies allegations it engaged in anti-competitive practices. A spokesman says Telekom does not require any private broadcaster to buy additional services as a condition for access to Telekom's cable network, as alleged in a complaint filed by the VPRT group of private television broadcasters. "We believe the complaint by the private broadcasters is unfounded," the spokesman says. The German cartel office said earlier it had begun an investigation based on the complaint. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The eastern state of Saxony plans to ask television viewers to vote on which stations should be included in the limited local cable network. "We want to require the cable companies to ask viewers what should have priority on cable television and what is less important," said Michael Sagurna, state government spokesman. (Frankfurter Rundschau)

WALLDORF - Public television network ZDF is a new investor in the Bavarian television film foundation (FFF), now providing six percent of the organisation's financial assistance to film makers. (Kress)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
HANOVER - Tyre manufacturer Continental AG says it expects a significant rise in net profit in full-year 1997 and that sales will rise about five percent to 11 billion marks ($6.4 billion).
(Reuter)

BONN - Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) propose raising taxes on petrol, tobacco and alcohol to fill Bonn's gaping budget holes and to help it qualify for the European Union's planned single currency, a newspaper says. The Handelsblat business daily, without naming its sources, says the CDU and its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), made the proposal at a crisis meeting of the coalition on Tuesday to find ways to balance the budget. (Reuter)

DARMSTADT - Haircare-product maker Wella AG says that it expected earnings in the current business year to increase by 25 percent, with sales set to rise by seven percent. Sales in April were 19 percent higher than in the previous year, while earnings growth thus far had also met expectations, management board chairman Joerg von Craushaar says at the group's annual meeting.
(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

WALLDORF - Christian Welzel will become chief executive of Revenue Management at the television advertising marketing company IP Deutschland in Kronberg, effective October 1. He leaves his post as director of sales and services at private channel Sat1. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Udo Vorstius has been tapped as the new chairman of the Thuringia Aufbaubank. He leaves the Deutsche Bank in Halle. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Michael Niemann, board member of Metro unit Oppermann Versand AG in Neumuenster, is now board spokesman. (Kress)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
